name: sites
description:
Show registered site identifiers in sorted order.

Returns:
    SitesResult: Unique site identifiers; `["MAIN"]` is supplied if the registry
    has no entries.

name: asset_ids
description:
Show the identifiers of assets registered at a site.

Choose `assets()` if you need registry metadata too.

Args:
    site_name: Supply an exact site identifier, e.g. `MAIN`; `sites()` can
        show which identifiers are valid.

Returns:
    AssetsResult: Asset identifiers sorted, plus the total count.

name: asset_detail
description:
Fetch one asset’s details from the registry.

Covers identity, type, description, location, status, installation date,
vintage plus the installed-sensor total. Get names with `installed_sensors()`.

Args:
    site_name: Supply an exact site identifier, e.g. `MAIN`; `sites()` can
        show which identifiers are valid.
    asset_id: Supply the exact identifier from `asset_ids()`, e.g. `Chiller 6`.

Returns:
    AssetDetail: Available fields from the registry; optional values become null
    if missing.

name: measured_sensors
description:
Show the measurement fields seen in asset telemetry.

Combines the entire stream into a sorted union, leaving out record metadata.
Choose `installed_sensors()` for assigned sensor names; those can differ.

Args:
    site_name: Supply an exact site identifier, e.g. `MAIN`; `sites()` can
        show which identifiers are valid.
    asset_id: Supply the exact identifier from `asset_ids()`, e.g. `Chiller 6`.

Returns:
    SensorsResult: Names of observed measurement fields, plus their count.

name: installed_sensors
description:
Show an asset’s registry-assigned sensor names.

Choose `measured_sensors()` for telemetry-observed fields; its list can
be different.

Args:
    site_name: Supply an exact site identifier, e.g. `MAIN`; `sites()` can
        show which identifiers are valid.
    asset_id: Supply the exact identifier from `asset_ids()`, e.g. `Chiller 6`.

Returns:
    SensorsResult: Names ordered as in the registry, plus their count.

name: assets
description:
Show a site’s assets with brief registry metadata.

Choose `asset_ids()` for just identifiers; `asset_detail()` supplies further fields
for an individual asset.

Args:
    site_name: Supply an exact site identifier, e.g. `MAIN`; `sites()` can
        show which identifiers are valid.
    assettype: Optional type filter requiring exact matching with case preserved, e.g.
        `PUMP`, alternatively `COMPRESSOR`.

Returns:
    AssetsWithMetadataResult: Entries ordered by identifier, including description,
    type, vintage plus the total of installed sensors.

name: find_assets_by_sensors
description:
Locate site assets using assigned or observed sensor names.

Only assets registered under `site_name` are searched. Repeated queries are
removed, retaining the order of their first occurrence.

Args:
    site_name: Supply an exact site identifier, e.g. `MAIN`; `sites()` can
        show which identifiers are valid.
    sensors: Names to search, or name fragments if `substring` is enabled.
    match: `all` needs each query; `any` needs one or more.
    substring: Match fragments without regard to case, replacing exact,
        case-sensitive comparison.
    source: `measured` checks observed fields; `installed` checks
        registry sensor assignments. The default is `measured`.

Returns:
    FindAssetsResult: Search settings and matched assets, including the actual
    sensor names that matched.

name: stream_extent
description:
Check asset telemetry record count and timestamp extent.

Optional filters select a measured sensor plus a ISO 8601 half-open interval:
`start` is included, whereas `end` is excluded. Sensor-filtered records qualify
only with that field non-null and present. Bounds and observation timestamps
must uniformly carry timezone offsets or uniformly omit them; aware timestamps undergo
comparison as instants, even with differing offsets.

Args:
    site_name: Supply an exact site identifier, e.g. `MAIN`; `sites()` can
        show which identifiers are valid.
    asset_id: Supply the exact identifier from `asset_ids()`, e.g. `Chiller 6`.
    sensor: An optional precise field name obtained through `measured_sensors()`.
        Reserved metadata names, including `asset_id` and `timestamp`, cannot be
        used as sensor identifiers.
    start: Optional lower boundary, included, as an date or datetime formatted using ISO 8601.
    end: Optional upper boundary, excluded, as an date or datetime formatted using ISO 8601.

Returns:
    StreamExtentResult: First and last qualifying timestamps, record
    count, an indication of whether it exceeds a page of 1000 records, and average
    spacing derived from the count and temporal extent.

name: history
description:
Fetch asset telemetry observations, one page ordered chronologically.

Optional bounds define a ISO 8601 half-open interval. Select using `sensors` the
precise measured fields; leave it out to include every measured field present per
row. Each row retains `asset_id` and `timestamp`, omitting all remaining record
bookkeeping metadata.

For page one, omit `cursor`. If `has_more` is true, resubmit the
identical query using `next_cursor`. Each cursor is opaque, tied to their query. Timestamp
offsets follow the rules of `stream_extent()`.

Args:
    site_name: Supply an exact site identifier, e.g. `MAIN`; `sites()` can
        show which identifiers are valid.
    asset_id: Supply the exact identifier from `asset_ids()`, e.g. `Chiller 6`.
    start: An optional ISO 8601 lower boundary, included.
    end: Optional ISO 8601 upper boundary, excluded.
    sensors: Optional list specifying precise measured names; it cannot be empty. Duplicate
        names are discarded, retaining their order.
    limit: Observation ceiling for this page, between 1 and 1000.
    cursor: The opaque `next_cursor` obtained on the preceding page for this identical query.

Returns:
    HistoryResult: Observations after projection, their count, bounds echoed back,
    and fields for advancing to the subsequent page.

name: latest_reading
description:
Fetch an asset’s most recent telemetry observation.

Leave `sensor` out to get every measured field of the latest record. If a sensor gets
specified, the tool selects the most recent record containing a non-null value in that field.
Parsed timestamps determine record order according to `stream_extent()`.

`age_seconds` subtracts the reading timestamp from UTC time now.
Offsetless timestamps are treated as UTC; negative age
means the observation timestamp lies ahead of now.

Args:
    site_name: Supply an exact site identifier, e.g. `MAIN`; `sites()` can
        show which identifiers are valid.
    asset_id: Supply the exact identifier from `asset_ids()`, e.g. `Chiller 6`.
    sensor: An optional precise field name obtained through `measured_sensors()`. Reserved
        metadata names cannot serve as sensors.

Returns:
    LatestReadingResult: Chosen timestamp and values, plus age measured in seconds.

name: sensor_coverage
description:
Summarize every measured sensor’s coverage of observations that are not null.

Scans the entire timestamped stream. `non_null_count` counts any present,
values that are non-null, irrespective of type. Exclusively null-valued fields receive zero
count with null boundaries. Timestamp offsets follow `stream_extent()`.

Args:
    site_name: Supply an exact site identifier, e.g. `MAIN`; `sites()` can
        show which identifiers are valid.
    asset_id: Supply the exact identifier from `asset_ids()`, e.g. `Chiller 6`.

Returns:
    SensorCoverageResult: Scanned timestamped-record total and counts per sensor
    with chronological boundaries, ordered by field name.

name: sensor_stats
description:
Calculate numerical summaries for one measured sensor or every measured sensor.

Leave `sensor` out to summarize each measured field. The optional bounds define a
ISO 8601 half-open interval. Timestamp offsets follow `stream_extent()`.

Finite numbers, including numeric strings, enter the numerical summaries.
Present booleans, nulls, non-finite and non-numeric values enter
`null_count`; absent fields enter neither count. Here, `stddev` denotes
population standard deviation: one numeric observation yields `0.0`; none yields null.

Args:
    site_name: Supply an exact site identifier, e.g. `MAIN`; `sites()` can
        show which identifiers are valid.
    asset_id: Supply the exact identifier from `asset_ids()`, e.g. `Chiller 6`.
    sensor: An optional precise field name obtained through `measured_sensors()`. Leave it out to
        summarize each measured field.
    start: Optional ISO 8601 lower boundary, included.
    end: Optional ISO 8601 upper boundary, excluded.

Returns:
    SensorStatsResult: Counts of numeric/null values per field, mean, range,
    population standard deviation, with first/last timestamps of numeric observations.

name: json_reader
description: Opens a file containing JSON, parses its contents, and supplies the resulting data.

name: get_sensor_catalog
description:
Fetch the sensor types in the catalog.

Entries include `sensor` plus `description`. Leave sensor out for every cataloged
sensor type, or supply sensor to find an exactly matching name.

name: get_asset_catalog
description:
Fetch asset classes with categories recorded in the catalog.

Entries include `category`, `category_description`, `asset`, plus
`description`. Leave filters out for the complete class catalog, or supply
asset, category, or both for exact matching.

name: get_failure_mode_catalog
description:
Fetch cataloged failure modes grouped by asset category.

These entries include `category`, `failure_mode`, plus `description`. Leave filters out
to enumerate every cataloged mode, or supply failure_mode, category, or both
to request exact matching.

name: current_date_time
description: Gives the present date and time in JSON representation.

name: current_time_english
description: Gives the present time using English wording.

name: get_failure_modes
description:
READ known failure modes associated with the specified class of assets.

Args:
    asset_class: Requested class, e.g. "pump". The tool normalizes case, whitespace,
        digits, hyphens and underscores before the lookup.

name: generate_failure_modes
description:
GENERATE failure modes associated with an asset class, starting or extending a list.

This tool makes no database writes. If normalized `asset_class`
is stored, its existing modes provide context
for the LLM to produce further modes. With no stored modes, the LLM
starts a fresh list.

Args:
    asset_class: Class to consider, e.g. "pump". The tool normalizes case,
        whitespace, digits, hyphens and underscores before
        sending the LLM prompt.
    max_modes: Upper limit on new failure modes requested from the LLM.

name: add_failure_modes
description:
WRITE an asset class’s failure modes into the database.

Preserves existing modes and merges incoming modes without case sensitivity,
reporting just the additions. Use when generated or curated
modes should be retrievable through later `get_failure_modes` retrieval.

Args:
    asset_class: Class to modify, e.g. "pump". The tool normalizes case, whitespace,
        digits, hyphens and underscores before saving.
    failure_modes: Modes being added for this asset class.
    exhaustive: Use true only if the stored set is believed complete. When
        unspecified, the prior value remains; newly created records default to false.
    source: Provenance, optionally attached to the stored set.

name: list_workorders
description:
Find work orders, optionally filtering by site, asset, status, priority or dates.
status allows OPEN / APPROVED_PENDING; setting page_size=0 retrieves every match together.

name: get_workorder
description: Fetch one work order using its number plus site.

name: get_workorder_tasks
description: Show subordinate tasks under one parent work order.

name: get_workorder_costs
description: Break down a work order’s actual spending: labor, material, service and tools.

name: get_workorder_actuals_vs_planned
description: Compare work-order estimates with actual hours and costs; give variances.

name: get_workorder_kpis
description: Site KPIs covering totals, backlog, overdue work, mean completion, priority/asset distributions.

name: get_schedule_calendar
description: Group scheduled work orders by day within a time window, excluding terminal ones.

name: get_my_assigned_workorders
description: Show work orders allocated to the specified technician’s labor code.

name: get_failure_codes
description:
Read the FCC catalog of failure codes stored in CouchDB.

Leave ``code`` unspecified to enumerate every available failure code; supply an exact code
like ``FC001`` for matching without case sensitivity; CouchDB metadata is excluded
from results.

name: generate_work_order
description: Open a work order with WAPPR status; attach agent/trigger/evidence provenance through aob_source.

name: update_workorder
description: Modify a work order’s editable fields.

name: approve_workorder
description: Authorize a work order, setting APPR.

name: assign_technician
description: Allocate a technician, adding one wplabor entry.

name: close_workorder
description: Complete a work order, setting COMP and recording actuals plus resolution.

name: cancel_workorder
description: Cancel the work order, setting CAN.
